event: VXE-425 (MARSOC, deployed) pitched nose down and crashed during the VTOL landing descent after lift power and current dropped to zero; aircraft destroyed.
failure_mode: ESC board burned and broke in two, 11 ohm short from input power to ground; lift system power and current fell to zero in the log
contributing: HLB connector excess potting service bulletin not applied
AS150 power contact 240 uohm, above the 235 uohm limit
known MOSFET lead corrosion issue on lift ESCs (VXEP-198) could not be checked
degraded GPS earlier in the flight

evidence.quote: Left aft ESC/motor not spinning up. Took cover off of ESC and it is quite cooked. 11 ohms measured between input power and ground
ESC PCBA destroyed, came out of enclosure in 2 pieces.
The data to me is consistent with the whole lift system losing power, but it’s possible one bad ESC could cause the others to lose power as well.
AS150 contact measured 240 uohms (limit is 235) before cleaning. After cleaning measured 205 uohms.
Could be that the failed ESC caused the attitude fault.

team_root_cause:
Causes:​
- Photos indicate that service bulletin was not applied to HLB (VXE-SB-23-002 HLB Mate Indicator Field Installation, Service Bulletin). This potting can interfere with the ability of the connector to fully mate, which can increase contact impedance, which increases voltage ripple at the ESCs, which increases current and stress on the soft start FETs.​
- Known issue about rust/corrosion on MOSFET leads used on lift ESCs, which increases impedance. Due to ESC damage, it is difficult to determine if this issue was present. https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/VXEP-198 ​
- Significant dam

would_settle_it.what: Lab failure analysis of the rear left ESC soft start FETs to tell an in-flight FET short from impact damage
Per-ESC current and throttle just before the power drop, to see whether one boom lost power first

attachments_read: 22832_RMA Repair Quote for AC VXE-425 Warranty MARSOC 8-30-2024.pdf.md
reasoning: Teardown found the left aft (rear left) ESC burned through with an 11 ohm input short while the other lift hardware and EC3/EC5 contacts were fine. The log shows the whole lift system losing power and current, and engineers could not tell whether the ESC failed first or was damaged at impact. The evidence points to the rear left ESC as the likely start, but it is not proven.
notes: Mark Squillante wrote 'Throttle 1 is left aft' per Cody, which conflicts with the VXEP-272 glossary (motor 4 = rear left); position uses the glossary and the physical finding 'left aft ESC'. VXEP-628 and VXEP-198 (general ESC and MOSFET trend tickets) were not read. RMA-218 intake PDF has no extractable text.

event: VXE-533 (USASOC training, Fort Moore) had a VTOL power fault at transition to VTOL landing, a failed abort, uncontrolled drift and crash into a tree line.
component: center wing voltage/current sensing circuit (dual current sense assembly 107-102264, CW autopilot, harness 107-102065, ground isolation board)
failure_mode: abnormal VTOL bus voltage sensing (Vref and AUX2 erratic, VBATT and BMS readings disagree) and power fault during transition to VTOL
contributing: VTOL abort race condition between APs (VXEP-283)
scuff mark and solder blobs on power connector, cause unclear
possible grounding issue

evidence.quote: There was a power fault that the FW AP triggered during transition to VTOL.
6/21 More data analysis, VBATT and BMS voltage readings are do not align during a certain time frame.
6/17 checked power connector and there was a scuff mark but unable to identify if it was dues to wear and tear or arching.
The power issue for this investigation was deemed inconclusive.
The issue is likely caused by one of these components or the battery.

team_root_cause:
Dave: “Grouped with 496”. Compound failure. Power failure led to VTOL abort. In both cases, stuck in a race condition between APs trying to control the vehicle. Building out test matrix to verify fixes for all applicable states. 
Specific components for power failure is undetermined however it has been isolated down to the voltage sensing circuitry: 1409P01D, 1901P01A1, 1911P01A, 107-102264, and 107-102065. Vref and AUX2 were behaving abnormally. Further testing can not be performed since the aircraft has been shipped back to the customer with new parts.

event: VXE-533 (USASOC training) aborted VTOL landing after a lift power fault, but the VTOL AP kept the lift motors running while in fixed wing mode, leading to uncontrolled drift and a crash.
failure_mode: race condition: after abort the VTOL AP returned to FW flight state but kept spooling the lift motors, so FW and VTOL APs fought for control
contributing: VTOL power fault at transition (VXEP-282) triggered the abort
abort took about 9 s to trigger

evidence.quote: They fight each other after that point because there is some sort of RACE condition in mode logic.
In this case the mode in the VTOL AP returned to FW flight. But it seems that didn't cut the lift system from trying to spool up.
HostState returns to FWFlight and then motors spool up, indicating a RACE condition within the VTOL AP.
This appears to be related to the bug that @Jason Scherer found while running HIL tests on Xkit.

team_view_in_comments: They start fighting each other once the abort is issued when the low power state is recognized.
reasoning: Log channels show the VTOL AP host state returning to FW flight while lift current rose, so both autopilots were flying the aircraft after the abort. FS2-1512 ties this to a race condition also seen in HIL testing and fixed in release 6.3.4. The power fault that started the abort is tracked separately in VXEP-282.
notes: Clone of VXEP-282 covering the abort logic only; no Root Cause field.

- The aircraft crashed because the FW AP was in idle state and never tried to fly the plane after VTOL AP transitioned to FW flight.

- Despite this, it is unclear if the aircraft should have passed through the launch wizard, in response to a COMMAND_SENSORHEALTH, an IMU error was detected and logged in the XCOMM log. This was seen multiple times, perhaps it was tried until it passed? We still need to document the exact Launch Wizard behavior here.

event: VXE-477 (MARSOC, deployed) transitioned to fixed wing after launch and crashed about two minutes later with airspeed reading too low; total loss.
failure_mode: pitot zeroed with pressure applied, so indicated airspeed read low; aircraft overspeeded and could not hold altitude in fixed wing flight
contributing: launch wizard allows launch with a bad pitot calibration
XCOMM preflight logging at 0.1 Hz cannot show the calibration moment
similar event on 2/12 that did not crash

evidence.quote: It looks to me like the air data system was reporting and airspeed that was too low.
After reviewing your summary and the VTOL logs, I believe this was user error.
I was also able to run a HIL test and reproduce a similar crash.
With XCOMM log events only written at 0.1Hz during preflight, it’s not possible to completely rule out operator error
as we dug into the investigation on 477 more it appeared to be user error (they pushed during both shield steps it looks like, see slide 6 here).

team_root_cause: Low airspeed measurement caused vehicle to fly too fast, resulting in not enough thrust to stay airborne.  User error caused pitot pressure to be applied during the shielding step, resulting in an incorrect pitot calibration.

would_settle_it.what: Slides 6 and 7 showing airspeed during both shield steps

attachments_read: 31288_001052 Rev. 1 MARSOC - RMA VXE-477 Misc. Parts.pdf.md
reasoning: Logs show the air data system reading airspeed too low after transition, so the aircraft flew too fast and lost altitude.
